text:
alex_support: FYI customer reports large latency and a ton of requests served from ap-southeast even though their failover policy is set to prefer eu-west. Billing spike noticed as well.
customer_corp: seeing 5xxs and much higher p95. HTTP response header shows x-desired-region: eu-west but x-served-region: ap-southeast most of the time. Why are we crossing regions?
maya_eng: can you paste the failover config they saved and any recent edits?
alex_support: pasted below — they edited via UI about an hour before the spike:
```
failover_policy: ["eu-west","us-east","ap-southeast"]
weights: [0.0,0.0,1.0]
sticky: true
```
jamie_sre: that weights array looks suspicious — if the parser treats those as strings or if the priority index order is inverted it could prefer the last non-zero weight. Also need route stamps from logs.
alex_support: log snippet from edge:```
2026-02-10T12:03:02Z route_eval request_id=ha12 desired_region=eu-west selected_region=ap-southeast reason=weight=1.0
2026-02-10T12:03:08Z route_eval request_id=ha13 desired_region=eu-west selected_region=ap-southeast reason=weight=1.0
```
maya_eng: repro steps I used locally — consistent with customer's repro: 1) curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "X-Client-Region: eu-west" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 2) inspect x-served-region header 3) repeat 50x. Result: ~90% served from ap-southeast.

maya_eng: hypothesis: UI serialization wrote weights as strings ("0","0","1") and parser's numeric coercion has a bug that flips priority when sticky routing is enabled.
linda_account: customer is asking for an immediate mitigation and credits, they're seeing extra egress costs.
jamie_sre: short mitigation: revert their policy to an earlier saved copy (we have snapshots). I've submitted revert at 12:20 UTC.
alex_support: applied revert to last-known-good at 12:20 UTC, live now.
deploy_bot: rollback job #9876 completed successfully (duration 6s).
customer_corp: after the revert latency is back to normal and region alignment looks correct, thanks. Billing still being audited on our side.
maya_eng: actionable follow-ups: 1) add strict type validation when loading weights (reject non-numeric), 2) add small detection alert if percent_served_in_preferred_region < 80% for 5m, 3) unit test for UI serializer->parser roundtrip, 4) run a targeted audit for saved policies with string-typed weights.
jamie_sre: I'll own the detection alert and incident playbook update. Filing SRE-2210.
maya_eng: I'll own the parser validation + unit tests, filing ENG-4482.
linda_account: I'll draft credit request and send incident notes to the customer, ticket CX-331.
alex_support: Customer confirmed resolution, marking this escalated issue as resolved for now :white_check_mark:. We should include the config snippet and log lines in the postmortem.
